title: Integrate benchmark matrix into benchmark-lab CI; publish artifacts with profile_version tags
creator: Talia Benson
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Context
- We’re shipping a versioned “hardware tuning profiles pack” in runtime-1.22. To safely iterate on defaults (kernel/scheduler/KV/memory knobs), we need reproducible benchmarks that run on CI (or CI-triggered lab runners) and persist results keyed by profile_version + git sha.
- Today we have ad-hoc runs (Drive sheets) and local scripts. We need benchmark-lab to be the source of truth, with artifacts stored and comparable across time.

Goal
- Integrate the benchmark matrix (workload buckets + models + concurrency) into benchmark-lab CI.
- Persist results and artifacts with consistent tagging:
  - profile_version (e.g., 1.0.0)
  - profile_id (e.g., h100-sxm-prod-default)
  - sku (H100/L40S/B200)
  - runtime git sha + benchmark-lab git sha
  - driver + CUDA version (and MIG mode if applicable)
  - workload bucket (short/medium/long context; mixed prefill/decode)

Scope (this ticket)
1) Benchmark matrix runner
- Encode matrix v1 (initially H100 + L40S; B200 smoke subset) as a checked-in config in benchmark-lab.
- Provide a CLI entrypoint to run:
  - single workload bucket
  - full matrix for a SKU
  - “PR smoke” subset (fast, deterministic)

2) CI integration
- Add CI workflow (Buildkite/GitHub Actions depending on benchmark-lab conventions) that:
  - runs schema validation on the matrix config
  - triggers lab execution on the appropriate GPU pools
  - uploads artifacts and a summary JSON to storage
- Initial stance: nightly + manual trigger; PR gating can come later via perf-canary/ENG-4930.

3) Artifacts + storage format
- Persist raw and summarized data:
  - raw per-request/per-stage latencies where feasible (or sampled)
  - aggregated p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory usage
  - counters: kernel fallback rate, scheduler queue time, OOM/evictions (where available)
- Store layout proposal (S3/GCS path semantics):
  - /benchmarks/runtime/{runtime_sha}/profile_pack/{profile_version}/sku/{sku}/date={YYYY-MM-DD}/run_id={uuid}/...
- Emit a machine-readable “results index” record per run for later dashboard ingestion.

4) Result comparability / metadata requirements
- Enforce required metadata fields for every run.
- Fail the run if:
  - profile_version missing
  - runtime cannot report active profile_id/sku
  - driver/CUDA cannot be detected
- Ensure environment metadata is captured in the artifact bundle.

Non-goals
- Defining acceptance thresholds and pass/fail gating logic (tracked in Confluence + perf-canary / ENG-4930).
- Building a full UI; we just need durable storage and stable schemas for Allison’s dashboards.

Implementation plan (proposed)
- Add `matrix/v1.yaml` checked into benchmark-lab repo (source of truth).
- Add runner command: `benchlab run-matrix --sku H100 --profile-version 1.0.0 --runtime-sha <sha> [--subset pr-smoke]`.
- Output files (per run):
  - `summary.json` (aggregates + metadata)
  - `metrics.ndjson` (optional raw)
  - `env.json` (host/GPU/driver/CUDA)
  - `logs.txt`
- Upload as a single bundle and also publish the `summary.json` to an index prefix for easy scanning.

Acceptance criteria
- A CI-triggered run can execute the H100 and L40S matrices (or defined subsets) against a pinned runtime build and produce a results bundle.
- Every results bundle includes:
  - profile_version, profile_id, sku, runtime_sha, benchmark_lab_sha, driver_version, cuda_version
  - workload bucket identifier
- Results are queryable via a stable path convention and an index file (per-run) suitable for dashboard ingestion.
- Document “How to run locally / how to trigger a lab run / how to find artifacts” in benchmark-lab README.

Risks / notes
- Noise: GPU pool variance and cross-region differences can swamp small deltas. For v1, focus on repeatability (fixed seeds, fixed ordering, warmup) and record enough metadata for later filtering.
- Cardinality: keep tags sane; do not include prompt IDs as metric labels.

Links
- Epic: ENG-4921
- Benchmark-lab PR: https://github.com/benchmark-lab/pull/913 (matrix runner + persistence)
- B200 smoke PR: https://github.com/benchmark-lab/pull/927 (allowed-to-fail initially)
- Perf gating follow-up: ENG-4930 / https://github.com/perf-canary/pull/388
- Runtime profile pack work (context): https://github.com/redwood/pull/24873, https://github.com/redwood/pull/24881

Split into buckets: (A) short prompt/short decode, (B) medium/medium, (C) long prompt/short decode, (D) mixed prefill/decode. Need confirmation from Claire that bucket distributions match the Confluence plan.

2026-02-14 (Rina Kobayashi): PR up in benchmark-lab (PR #913). Includes: YAML matrix, `benchlab run-matrix`, artifact bundle upload, and per-run index JSON. Pending: CI trigger wiring + docs updates. Also added env capture (nvidia-smi + CUDA runtime).

2026-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): Reviewed PR #913. Requesting: (1) deterministic seed handling surfaced in CLI, (2) ensure runtime build identifier is recorded even if runtime sha isn’t available (e.g., local build), (3) add schema validation step in CI to fail fast on malformed matrix config.
